'''Ishii Shrine''' (石井神社) is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Niigata Prefecture|Niigata Prefecture]], [[Mishima District (Niigata)|Mishima District]], [[Izumozaki, Niigata|Izumozaki Town]], Ishiimachi. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} {{ill|Disputed shrine|ja|論社|1=candidate shrines|2=ja|3=論社|lt=candidate|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Disputed shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/candidate shrines|qq=}}. The shrine is regarded as the total shrine of Izumozaki Town. Its former Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=this used to link to modern system but that one is too overlinked|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} was {{ill|Village shrine|ja|村社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}.
== Overview ==
The founding date of the shrine is unknown. According to legend, during the {{ill|Age of the gods (Japanese mythology)|ja|神代|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Age of the gods (Japanese mythology)|qq=}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}}, who sought to pacify {{ill|Sado Island|en|Sado Island|qid=Q998623|lt=Sado Island|1=Sado Island}}, sprinkled water from a stone well, causing twelve sacred trees to grow overnight. These trees were used to construct a ship to cross to Sado. A great deity of maritime protection was enshrined at the site of these sacred trees, known as Iibana. For this reason, the shrine was originally called {{ill|Jūnisho Shrine|ja|十二所神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jūnisho Shrine|qq=}}. During the {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period|1=Nara period}}, prayers by the {{ill|Sado bugyō|en|Sado bugyō|qid=Q4274645|lt=Sado governor|1=Sado bugyō}} calmed a storm, enabling safe return. This increased faith in the shrine, which was relocated from {{ill|Mt. Jūni|ja|十二山|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mt. Jūni|qq=}} in Kanazawa Village to its current site in 712 CE (Wadō 4).<ref name="Izumozaki Hoketsu">{{Cite news |title=Izumozaki: Hoketsu Materials |newspaper=Sato Bookstore |date=1906-09-01 |author=Nishizawa Shinji (ed.) |page=}}</ref>
== Auxiliary Shrines ==
* {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine|en|Sumiyoshi Shrine|qid=Q32512|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine|1=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} ({{ill|Auxiliary shrine|ja|Keigai-Sessha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Auxiliary shrine|qq=}})
== Festivals ==
Since 1690 CE (Genroku 3), the shrine has held the {{ill|Maritime Safety Prayer Festival|ja|海上安全祈願祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maritime Safety Prayer Festival|qq=}} on June 17–18. Later, this was conducted jointly with other shrines, and in 2010 (Heisei 22), it was renamed the {{ill|Izumozaki Grand Festival|ja|出雲崎大祭|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumozaki Grand Festival|qq=}}. A mikoshi procession visits Ryōkandō, Anase, Iibana, and returns to Ryōkandō.
== Visitor Information ==
'''Access'''
* Rail: From {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|en|East Japan Railway Company|qid=Q499071|lt=JR East|1=East Japan Railway Company}} [[Izumozaki Station]], [[Kashiwazaki Station]], or [[Nagaoka Station]], take the {{ill|Echigo Kotsu|en|Echigo Kotsu|qid=Q11636491|lt=Echigo Kotsu|1=Echigo Kotsu}} bus bound for Izumozaki Garage and alight at "Ryōkandō-mae" bus stop.
